subject: Life Skills
title: The Halo Effect
description: A fast breakdown of The Halo Effect for builders.

hook.text: Attractive defendants receive lighter sentences in court. Jurors assume good looks mean good character.

buildup.text: Edward Thorndike named the halo effect in 1920. One positive trait bleeds into our judgment of everything else.

discovery.text: If someone is funny, you unconsciously assume they are also smart, kind, and trustworthy. The halo distorts everything.

twist.text: The reverse exists too. One negative trait — rudeness, for example — makes you rate their competence lower unfairly.

climax.text: Slow down your judgments. Ask yourself: 'Am I evaluating this person or reacting to one standout trait?'

punchline.text: One bright trait blinds you to the rest. Look harder.

quiz.question: What is the halo effect?
options: People with halos in photos are judged more positively
One positive trait causes you to assume other positive traits exist
Bright lighting makes people appear more trustworthy
